'''Jay Van Andel''' (June 3, 1924 – December 7, 2004) was an American billionaire businessman, best known as co-founder of the [[Amway]] Corporation, along with [[Richard DeVos]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/news/grand-rapids/2019/09/amways-60th-anniversary-seeks-to-build-on-its-pioneering-spirt.html|title=Amway's 60th anniversary seeks to build on its 'pioneering spirit|last=|first=|date=2019-09-10|website=MLive|access-date=}}</ref>

He also served as chairman of the [[United States Chamber of Commerce|U.S. Chamber of Commerce]] from 1979 to 1980.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amwayglobal.com/our-story/founders/|title=Amway Founders|last=|first=|date=|website=Amway|access-date=}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Jay Van Andel was born on June 3, 1924, to James and Petronilla (Van der Woude) Van Andel in Grand Rapids, Michigan.<ref>{{Cite book|title=An Enterprising Life|last=Van Andel|first=Jay|publisher=Harper Business - Zondervan Publishing House|year=1998|isbn=0-88730-997-6|location=New York, NY|pages=2}}</ref> His grandparents, Christian and Elizabeth had immigrated to America from the Netherlands in 1909.<ref>{{Cite book|title=An Enterprising Life|last=Van Andel|first=Jay|publisher=Harper Business - Zondervan Publishing Company|year=1998|isbn=0-88730-997-6|location=New York, NY|pages=2}}</ref>

Van Andel's parents were devout Christians and members of the [[Christian Reformed Church in North America|Christian Reformed Church]]. Jay credits his Christian background as being foundational for the rest of his life as a Christian. He once wrote, "Christianity involved the living out of Biblical values of honesty, generosity, and respect for others in our everyday life."<ref>{{Cite book|title=An Enterprise Life|last=Van Andel|first=Jay|publisher=Harper Business - Zondervan Publishing|year=1998|isbn=0-88730-997-6|location=New York, NY|pages=3}}</ref>

Jay attended [[Grand Rapids Christian High School]]. Later, Van Andel attended [[Calvin University (Michigan)|Calvin College]] and Pratt Business School in Kansas.

When [[World War II]] broke out, Jay served as a [[United States Army Air Forces|United States Army Air Force]] officer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amwayglobal.com/our-story/founders/|title=Amway Founders|last=|first=|date=|website=Amway|access-date=}}</ref> He was commissioned as a second lieutenant and trained crews for B-17 and B-29 bombers that reached the Japanese mainland.<ref>{{Cite book|title=An Enterprising Life|last=Van Andel|first=Jay|publisher=Harper Business - Zondervan Publishing House|year=1998|isbn=0-88730-997-6|location=New York, NY|pages=13}}</ref>

Jay met his wife Betty Jean Hoekstra while on a direct selling house call in the spring of 1951. They married on August 16, 1952.<ref>{{Cite book|title=An Enterprising Life|last=Van Andel|first=Jay|publisher=Harper Business - Zondervan Publishing House|year=1998|isbn=0-88730-997-6|location=New York, NY|pages=201–202}}</ref>

== Amway ==
While attending the Grand Rapids Christian High School before World War II, Jay Van Andel met Rich DeVos.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amwayglobal.com/our-story/founders/|title=Amway Founders|last=|first=|date=|website=Amway|access-date=}}</ref> In 1949, Van Andel and DeVos became distributors of [[Nutrilite]] dietary supplements. They added cleaning products including Liquid Organic Cleaner, to their core line of products in 1958. In 1959, the "American Way Association" began in the basements of the Van Andel and DeVos homes, and later that year "Amway Sales Corporation" was formed. A converted service station became Amway's first outside office building in 1960.<ref name="enterprising">''An Enterprising Life'', by Jay Van Andel</ref>

Today, [[Amway]] is a direct selling multinational company that sells a variety of health, beauty, and home care products. Amway went on to become the largest direct selling company in the world.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.inc.com/emily-richett/the-3-beliefs-every-leader-should-adopt-from-one-of-worlds-wealthiest-self-made-entrepreneurs.html|title=One of the Wealthiest Self-Made Entrepreneurs Ever Believed in These 3 Things|last=|first=|date=2019-04-22|website=Inc. Magazine|access-date=}}</ref> Amway corporate reports that in 2019, they have over 3 million independent business owners (IBOs) in over 100 countries.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amway.com/about-amway/business-opportunity|title=Become a IPO|last=|first=|date=|website=Amway|access-date=|archive-date=2019-06-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190616132433/https://www.amway.com/about-amway/business-opportunity|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Van Andel Institute ==
In 1996, Van Andel founded [[Van Andel Institute]] with his wife Betty.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vai.org/about-us/|title=Van Andel Institute About Us page|last=|first=|date=|website=Van Andel Institute|access-date=}}</ref> The [[501(c)(3)]] nonprofit organization is located in [[Grand Rapids, Michigan]], and focuses on disease research and science education. Researchers look for ways to better diagnose and treat diseases, primarily [[cancer]] and [[neurodegenerative diseases]] such as [[Parkinson's]]. Education programs seek to inspire and prepare students to become the next generation of researchers.<ref>{{cite web |publisher = Charity Navigator |title=Van Andel Institute |url= http://www.charitynavigator.org/index.cfm?bay=search.summary&orgid=6245 |accessdate = August 23, 2012}}</ref>

Since 1996, the Van Andel Institute is led by Jay's son, David Van Andel, as chairman and CEO.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-10-05 |title=Highlights of Hope 20th Anniversary Edition by Van Andel Institute - Issuu |url=https://issuu.com/vanandelinstitute9/docs/final_20th_ann._highlights_of_hope_ |access-date=2023-05-18 |website=issuu.com |language=en |archive-date=2023-05-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230518035740/https://issuu.com/vanandelinstitute9/docs/final_20th_ann._highlights_of_hope_ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Political activity and philanthropy ==
A strong supporter of the [[United States Republican Party|Republican Party]], in 2004 Van Andel contributed $2 million to [[Progress for America]], a [[527 organization|527 committee]] (sometimes referred to as [[political action committee]]) established in 2001 to support the re-election campaign of President [[George W. Bush]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jay van Andel Contributions to 527 Organizations, 2004 cycle {{!}} OpenSecrets |url=https://www.opensecrets.org/527s/527indivsdetail.php?id=U0000000010&cycle=2004 |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=www.opensecrets.org}}</ref> In that same year, he donated $475,000 to the Michigan State Republican Party (mostly for state legislature candidates).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Donor Lookup |url=https://www.opensecrets.org/donor-lookup/results?cand=&cycle=&employ=Amway&name=&order=desc&sort=A&state=&zip= |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=OpenSecrets |language=en}}</ref> He was noted for his friendship with former President [[Gerald R. Ford]], a native of [[Grand Rapids, Michigan|Grand Rapids]], who lamented his death and called him "a great family man and a worldwide leader in the business arena".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2004-12-08 |title=Amway co-founder dies at 80 |url=https://www.smh.com.au/business/amway-co-founder-dies-at-80-20041209-gdka07.html |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |language=en}}</ref> [[Steve Forbes]] wrote, "Whether in business or philanthropy, Van Andel understood that the primary goal was to serve the needs and wants of other people. He exemplified the best of America".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2005-02-04 |title=Forbes.com - Magazine Article |website=[[Forbes]] |url=http://www.forbes.com/forbes/2005/0214/025_print.html |access-date=2023-05-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050204042939/http://www.forbes.com/forbes/2005/0214/025_print.html |archive-date=2005-02-04 }}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 1981, Van Andel received the Golden Plate Award of the [[Academy of Achievement|American Academy of Achievement]].<ref>{{cite web|title= Golden Plate Awardees of the American Academy of Achievement |website=www.achievement.org|publisher=[[American Academy of Achievement]]|url=https://achievement.org/our-history/golden-plate-awards/#business}}</ref>

In 1993, Jay Van Andel was honored with an [[Edison Awards|Edison Achievement Award]] for his commitment to innovation throughout his career.

== Death ==
Van Andel and his wife Betty both died in 2004; Betty had [[Alzheimer's disease]], and Jay had [[Parkinson's]].<ref>{{cite web |publisher = Encyclopedia of World Biography |title=Jay Van Andel |url= http://www.notablebiographies.com/newsmakers2/2006-Ra-Z/Van-Andel-Jay.html |accessdate = August 23, 2012}}</ref> He was 80.
